author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can narrow the veterinarian list to one specialty by URL
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces accept an optional specialty in the URL and list only the veterinarians holding it, matched on the whole name ignoring letter case. The HTML page paginates the narrowed list and its page links keep the specialty; the machine-readable list is reinstated as a supported surface under REQ-VET-004.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only the veterinarians holding that specialty; each listed veterinarian still shows every specialty they hold.
[REQ-VET-003] GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only the veterinarians holding that specialty.
[REQ-VET-003] Matching is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case, on both surfaces: SURGERY and Surgery match surgery; a prefix such as surg matches no veterinarian.
[REQ-VET-003] A specialty no veterinarian holds yields HTTP 200 with the normal HTML page or JSON document and an empty veterinarian list, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces.

[REQ-VET-003] On /vets.html, pagination applies to the filtered list: the page count and each page's contents reflect matching veterinarians only, and every pagination link carries the specialty parameter.
[REQ-VET-003] A veterinarian holding no specialty never appears in a filtered result on either surface.
[REQ-VET-003] Case-insensitive matching holds on every supported database, not only the default one.
[REQ-VET-003] Without the parameter both surfaces behave as today: /vets.html lists every veterinarian a page at a time, and /vets returns every veterinarian in one document.
[REQ-VET-004] GET /vets without the parameter returns every veterinarian with the specialties each holds.
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty, on either surface (owner: 'Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control in this request').
Free-text veterinarian search (NG-9 as narrowed: 'free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope').
Filtering by any attribute other than specialty; NG-9 now admits other shown attributes, but the request names only specialty.
Narrowing by more than one specialty in one request; the request names a single specialty. Recorded as a PRD open question.
Any rule for spaces around a non-blank specialty value; the request settles only an empty or whitespace-only value. Left unspecified; recorded as a PRD open question.
Any on-page indication of the active filter; the request makes the filter a URL contract only. Recorded as a PRD open question.
Paging the machine-readable list; without the parameter it behaves as today and returns every veterinarian at once.
New user-facing wording, including a no-match message; a specialty no veterinarian holds yields the normal page with an empty list.
notes: REQ mapping: REQ-VET-003 is the specialty filter across both surfaces; REQ-VET-004 is the fresh requirement the owner asked for when reinstating the JSON surface (intake decision 2). REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn; its Superseded entry no longer says the route is pending removal. REQ-VET-004's single bullet ships in this slice under the batching rule: alone it is one cycle and only makes sense beside the filter. Its test may extend the existing showResourcesVetList test, which today asserts only the first id; the implementer's walk names the carrying test. Test names are one per behavior; each may be data-driven over surfaces or letter-case variants. PRD edge cases 3-5 of the Veterinarian directory are new; edge case 2 is struck as resolved. Precedent for acceptance criterion 8: owner search is case-insensitive under H2 and MySQL but not PostgreSQL (Owner records edge case 3). Doc follow-ups outside this agent's write scope: docs/system-design.md still records the machine-readable route as serving no requirement and pending removal (Contracts rows for Vets and VetController, and the gaps table), which is for system-design-expert; docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-09-11-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure) and follows the owner-search seam: a paged Spring Data derived query from a caller-supplied string, and blank input treated as no narrowing (OwnerController processFindForm, OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith). Two parts are new and now recorded. First, case-insensitive matching folds case in the query on both sides, compared by equality, so it is identical on H2, MySQL and PostgreSQL whatever the column type (specialties.name is VARCHAR in H2, TEXT in PostgreSQL, ci-collated in MySQL): system-design § Persistence plus ADR 2026-09-11-case-insensitive-matching-folds-case-in-the-query. Second, narrowed reads are not cached, so no caller-chosen value becomes a key in the unbounded vet cache: Contracts VetRepository row plus ADR 2026-09-11-narrowed-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache. REQ-VET-004 reinstates /vets unchanged in shape: Vets, VetController and VetRepository rows now cite it, and the Known Defects row for the unused route is gone. Basis: grep and file reads of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Vets, vetList.html, CacheConfiguration and the three schema.sql files; the IDE oracle is not connected, so this is the weaker basis. No module boundary, service layer or dependency change.
integration_points: Binding, both entry points: GET /vets.html and GET /vets each bind specialty as an optional request-scoped String query parameter (@RequestParam(required = false)). No persisted type is bound. The mass-assignment disallow list covers request-bound types, so a scalar parameter needs no binder (security-principles § Realization, Mass assignment row).

Double, repository boundary: the real VetRepository over the seeded H2 database. Matching lives in the query, so a Mockito stub of VetRepository cannot carry the letter-case, prefix, no-specialty, empty-result or page-count tests (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, real objects first). Drive these through MockMvc over a full application context (@SpringBootTest plus @AutoConfigureMockMvc). Either convert VetControllerTests, or add a sibling test class in the vet package if the existing @WebMvcTest tests keep their tolerated Mockito stubs.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Multi-page narrowed test data: the seed has at most two holders per specialty and the page size is five. The pagination test inserts extra vets and vet_specialties rows inside its own rolled-back transaction (@Sql or JdbcTemplate under @Transactional; testing-principles § Automate Persistent Cleanup). No production write path for veterinarians is added.

Cross-vendor evidence for the every-database criterion: add one mixed-case narrowed repository read each to MySqlIntegrationTests and PostgresIntegrationTests. They run against real databases and skip without Docker; no double.

VetRepository: two narrowed read methods that mirror the existing findAll pair, one paged for /vets.html and one whole for /vets. Both @Transactional(readOnly = true), neither @Cacheable (ADR 2026-09-11-narrowed-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache). Unnarrowed findAll methods stay unchanged and cached.

VetController: an absent or blank (String.isBlank) value takes the existing unnarrowed calls unchanged. A non-blank value goes to the narrowed calls unchanged, with no trimming, because the PRD leaves surrounding spaces open. The effective specialty (null when unnarrowed) joins the pagination model for link building. Narrowing is request adaptation plus delegation, not a controller rule (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row).

vetList.html: every pagination link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries the specialty only when narrowed; unnarrowed links render as today. No on-page filter indication and no new message keys (PRD REQ-VET-003 non-goals; REQ-LANG-002).
GET /vets narrowed returns the same Vets document with the narrowed vetList; no match gives HTTP 200 with an empty vetList.

patterns.description: paged derived query driven by a caller-supplied string
blank search input normalized to the broadest search before delegation
findPaginated and addPaginationModel: the pagination model the narrowed page reuses
read-only transactional findAll pair, paged and whole, that the narrowed pair mirrors minus @Cacheable

risks.risk: Template expression injection. The existing links build URLs with preprocessing (__${i}__). A specialty put through that form is evaluated as a Thymeleaf/SpEL expression, which gives caller-controlled code execution.
risks.mitigation: Pass the specialty only as a link-expression parameter, @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}; the engine URL-encodes it. Never place a request-derived value inside __...__ (system-design § Threat Model, template expression injection row).

risks.risk: Null-valued link parameter. Thymeleaf can render a parameter whose value is null as a bare name, which would change the unnarrowed links.
risks.mitigation: Emit the specialty parameter only when narrowed. Assert that unnarrowed pages still render today's link hrefs (PRD REQ-VET-003 criterion on behaving as today).

risks.risk: A join fetch on the filter condition trims each veterinarian's specialty set to the matched one, which breaks 'still shows every specialty they hold'.
risks.mitigation: Filter with a plain join or an exists/member-of condition, and let specialties load through the existing eager mapping (system-design § Persistence, eager associations; PRD edge case 4).

risks.risk: Duplicate rows and inflated page counts. specialties.name is not unique on any vendor, and H2's vet_specialties has no unique constraint, so a collection join can return one veterinarian twice.
risks.mitigation: Use a distinct result and a distinct count (findDistinctBy... or explicit select distinct). The page count then counts matching veterinarians only (system-design § Persistence, schemas not constraint-identical).

risks.risk: Pattern or collation matching. Like, Containing or StartingWith lets surg match surgery and treats % and _ as wildcards. Relying on column collation leaves H2 and PostgreSQL case-sensitive.
risks.mitigation: Compare by equality with case folded on both sides in the query, via IgnoreCase in a derived query or lower()/upper() on both sides in JPQL (ADR 2026-09-11-case-insensitive-matching-folds-case-in-the-query; system-design § Persistence).

risks.risk: Filtering in the controller (findAll then an in-memory filter) breaks page counts and adds a business rule to a web controller.
risks.mitigation: Narrow in the repository query only (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; § Design Validation Checklist).

risks.risk: Cache growth and test pollution. A @Cacheable added for symmetry lets caller values grow the unbounded vet cache. Separately, a test that inserts veterinarians and then reads unnarrowed pages leaves rolled-back rows cached in the shared test context.
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on narrowed reads (ADR 2026-09-11-narrowed-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache; system-design § Threat Model, cache-growth row). Tests that insert rows use only narrowed reads, or evict the vets cache (testing-principles § Never Share Mutable Fixtures).

risks.risk: Unordered pages. Neither the unnarrowed nor the narrowed page carries an ORDER BY, so asserting page contents by position is fragile.
risks.mitigation: The pagination test asserts membership and counts: every listed veterinarian holds the specialty, the total pages match, and the pages together cover the matching set. It does not assert order, and adding a sort is out of scope (testing-principles § Derived Expectations).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Doc follow-ups from the prd-entry notes are done: the Contracts rows for Vets, VetController and VetRepository cite REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004, the Known Defects row for the unused route is replaced by a resolution sentence, and docs/adr/README.md has index rows for the NG-9 non-goal ADR and the two new ADRs. Security Context inputs and two Threat Model rows are marked designed, not derived, to keep the section's provenance. Brief gap for the security-principles owner (outside this agent's write scope): § Realization has no row for template expression injection via preprocessing, and none for resource exhaustion through caller-keyed caches. Both are recorded only in system-design § Threat Model. Harness text defect: the agent definition and adr-template allow a one-clause rationale on a current-state line, but design-validation's pre-handoff self-check bars causal clauses in system-design.md. This dispatch followed the stricter rule and moved rationale into ADRs. Doctor check passes (0 failures).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty reaches the database only through Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java diff: `Page<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialty, Pageable pageable)` and its Collection overload), which bind it as a parameter and compare by upper-cased equality, never LIKE, so `%`/`_` stay literal. A sweep of the added diff lines for `@Query|createQuery|nativeQuery` returned no hits.

Template expression injection: the change removes the `__${...}__` preprocessing from every vetList.html pagination link (old: `th:href="@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}"`). The specialty now reaches links only as a link-expression parameter (new: `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), which Thymeleaf URL-encodes, and then as an attribute value, which it HTML-escapes. `grep -rnF -e 'specialty' src/main/resources/templates/` shows no other render of the request value. Line 20 iterates the entity's `specialty.name` via th:text, which is escaped. VetControllerTests.java:103 pins this with the `'+${7*7}+'` probe.

XSS: no `th:utext` or `[(` unescaped inlining in the added lines (grep of the added diff lines returned no hit). The JSON route returns the same `Vets` type as before, with no new fields and no Jackson polymorphic typing added (grep of the added lines for `JsonTypeInfo` returned no hit).

Resource exhaustion: the narrowed reads carry no `@Cacheable` (VetRepository.java diff: `Not cached, so a caller-chosen name never becomes a cache key`), so distinct caller-chosen values cannot grow the `vets` cache. This matches the system-design Threat Model row and its ADR. The page-number cache key on unnarrowed reads is pre-existing, is recorded there, and this change does not widen it.

Boundary validation: the blank/absent specialty collapses to no narrowing through `Optional.ofNullable(specialty).filter(name -> !name.isBlank())` (VetController.java diff). Any other value is legal under the REQ-VET-003 contract (an unheld name yields an empty list, not a refusal), and the servlet container bounds the query-string length. No new request-bound object, `@ModelAttribute`, or `@RequestBody` is introduced, so there is no mass-assignment surface. No new endpoint: both routes pre-exist and gain one optional read-only parameter, with no state mutation and no logging of the value.

Secrets: a case-insensitive sweep of the added diff lines for `password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential|private.?key|jdbc:` matched only system-design.md prose describing existing environment-variable credentials. No credential is added in source, tests, or config.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set (`scripts/changeset.sh --name-only`), so no dependency is added or changed. `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, jackson-databind (tools.jackson.core) 3.1.5, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE and Hibernate ORM 7.4.5.Final. No NVD match ran: `grep -nF -e 'dependencyCheck' build.gradle` returned nothing, so dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured, and this review has no network access.

author: change-grader
summary: filter the vet list by specialty on both surfaces

blast_radius.note: Production reach is three files in the vet feature (controller, repository, list template), with no schema, config, build, or sensitive-path change. Most of the 61 hunks are the rewritten VetControllerTests and doc edits that match the intake decisions.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do what the request says. A blank value collapses to the unchanged unnarrowed calls. The derived query compares by case-folded equality with no LIKE and has no @Cacheable. All five page links drop __${...}__ preprocessing for link-expression parameters (no __ remains in vetList.html), and unnarrowed links still render /vets.html?page=N, which a test pins. The loop variable named specialty on line 20 shadows the new model attribute only inside the row, away from the links.

test_adequacy.note: The core tests are real: real H2 via MockMvc, letter-case and prefix/wildcard variants, blank handling, a pagination test with inserted rows, and a '+${7*7}+' injection probe on the links. Two gaps remain. The every-database case-fold criterion rests on MySQL and PostgreSQL tests that skip without Docker, and build/test-results has no result file for either class, so that evidence did not run here. The duplicate-name test's totalItems=1 assertion cannot catch a non-distinct count query, because Spring Data skips the count query when the first page is short. That leaves the design's inflated-page-count risk unpinned.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved in round 1, and the citations I checked resolve (VetControllerTests.java:103, system-design.md lines 18/183/221, ubiquitous-language.md lines 50/52). Two mild caveats remain. code-quality left a clarify finding on the five duplicated specialty ternaries in vetList.html:33-58, the lines that carry the injection defense. test-reviewer calls the cross-vendor case-fold 'independently verified' on MySQL and PostgreSQL, but those tests did not execute. The missing NVD scan is a standing project gap, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, consultations, and build retries. The diff stays inside the intake: both surfaces are URL-only with no control, and pagination links carry the parameter. NG-9 is narrowed via an ADR, REQ-VET-004 is minted with REQ-VET-002 still withdrawn, and the three open questions are recorded rather than decided. The switch of VetControllerTests to @SpringBootTest is sanctioned by the design block.

rationale: The production change is small and reads as intended. The query uses case-folded equality, narrowed reads are uncached, and preprocessing is gone from every page link. Before merging, confirm the MySQL and PostgreSQL case-fold tests have actually run somewhere, since they skipped here without Docker. Also accept that no test pins the distinct page count on a multi-page result.
